source_text: Christus Iesus, dominus noster, permittat dicere interim, quisquis est, cuiuscunque dei filius, cuiuscunque materiae homo et deus, cuiuscunque fidei praeceptor, cuiuscunque mercedis repromissor, quid esset,quid fuisset, quam patris voluntatem administraret, quid homini agendum determinaret, quamdiu in terris agebat, ipse pronuntiabat sive populo palam sive discentibus seorsum, ex quibus duodecim praecipuos lateri suo allegerat, destinatos nationibus magistros. Itaque uno eorum decusso reliquos undecim digrediens ad patrem post resurrectionem iussit ire et docere nationes tinguendas in patrem et in filium et in spiritum sanctum. Statim igitur apostoli, quos haec appellatio missos interpretatur, assumpto per sortem duodecimo Matthia in locum Iudae ex auctoritate prophetiae, quae est in psalmo David, consecuti promissam vim spiritus sancti ad virtutes et eloquium, primo per Iudaeam contestata fide in Iesum Christum et ecclesiis institutis, dehinc in orbem profecti eandem doctrinam eiusdem fidei nationibus promulgaverunt. Et perinde ecclesias apud unamquamque civitatem condiderunt, a quibus traducem fidei et semina doctrinae ceterae exinde ecclesiae mutuatae sunt et cottidie mutuantur, ut ecclesiae fiant. Ac per hoc et ipsae apostolicae deputabuntur ut suboles apostolicarum ecclesiarum. Omne genus ad originem suam censeatur necesse est. Itaque tot ac tantae ecclesiae una est illa ab apostolis prima, ex qua omnes. Sic omnes primae et omnes apostolicae, dum una omnes probant unitate communicatio pacis et appellatio fraternitatis et contesseratio hospitalitatis, quae iura non alia ratio regit quam eiusdem sacramenti una traditio.
thought_title: The apostolic origin and unity of the churches
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the true faith and the Scriptures belong to the apostolic churches, and here he traces how Christ's teaching was handed down through the apostles to the churches they founded.
pass_a_gloss: Christ Jesus, our Lord, may he permit me to say for the present, whoever he is, son of whatever god, man and god of whatever matter, teacher of whatever faith, promiser of whatever reward, what he was, what he had been, what will of the Father he was carrying out, what he was determining for man to do, while he was living on earth, he himself was declaring either openly to the people or separately to the disciples, from whom he had chosen twelve chief ones for his side, destined as teachers for the nations. And so when one of them had been struck off, the remaining eleven, departing to the Father after the resurrection, he ordered to go and teach the nations, to be baptized into the Father and into the Son and into the Holy Spirit. Immediately therefore the apostles, whom this name interprets as 'sent ones', having taken by lot the twelfth Matthias into the place of Judas from the authority of the prophecy which is in the psalm of David, having obtained the promised power of the Holy Spirit for miracles and speech, first having testified to the faith in Jesus Christ throughout Judea and having established churches, then having set out into the world they proclaimed the same teaching of the same faith to the nations. And in the same way they founded churches in each city, from which the other churches thereafter borrowed the shoot of faith and the seeds of teaching, and borrow daily, so that they become churches. And through this they themselves also will be counted as apostolic, as offspring of apostolic churches. Every kind must be judged by its origin. And so all those many and great churches are that one first church from the apostles, from which all come. Thus all are first and all are apostolic, while all prove themselves one by the unity of the sharing of peace and the name of brotherhood and the exchange of hospitality, which rights no other reason governs than the one tradition of the same sacrament.

choices.why: tradux literally means a vine-layer or shoot for propagation; the image is of churches deriving their faith as a living offshoot from the apostolic churches
semina is plural and concrete, matching the agricultural metaphor of traducem
suboles means offspring or progeny, continuing the botanical/genealogical metaphor
contesseratio refers to the mutual exchange of tokens (tesserae) that established a bond, here the mutual recognition of hospitality between churches
traditio is the glossary term for the teaching handed down; una emphasizes the single shared tradition

pass_b_english: May Christ Jesus our Lord permit me to say this for the moment, whoever he is, of whatever god he is the son, of whatever substance he is man and God, of whatever faith he is the teacher, of whatever reward he is the promiser: what he was, what he had been, what will of the Father he was carrying out, what he determined man should do, he himself was declaring all this while he lived on earth, whether openly to the people or privately to his disciples, from whom he had chosen twelve chief men to be at his side, destined as teachers for the nations.

And so when one of them was struck off, he ordered the remaining eleven, as he was departing to the Father after his resurrection, to go and teach the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).

Immediately, then, the apostles, a name that means sent ones, took Matthias by lot as the twelfth in place of Judas, according to the authority of the prophecy in the psalm of David (Acts 1:26; Psalm 109:8), and having obtained the promised power of the Holy Spirit for miracles and speech (Acts 2:4), they first testified to faith in Jesus Christ throughout Judea and established churches, and then went out into the world and proclaimed the same teaching of the same faith to the nations.

In the same way they founded churches in each city, from which the other churches afterward borrowed the shoot of faith and the seeds of teaching, and still borrow them daily, so that they become churches.
And for this reason they too will be counted as apostolic, as offspring of apostolic churches.
Every kind of thing must be judged by its origin.
And so all those churches, many and great as they are, are that one first church from the apostles, from which all the rest come.

Thus all are first and all are apostolic, while all together prove their unity by the communion of peace, the name of brotherhood, and the exchange of hospitality, rights which no other principle governs than the one tradition of the same sacred mystery.

polish.changed: Clarified the flow of the argument by breaking long sentences into shorter, more natural units, making the subject of each clause explicit, and smoothing the transition from Christ's teaching to the apostles' mission and the spread of the churches.

notes.why: 'Nations' and 'Gentiles' alternate for the same concept without explanation.
notes.fix: Use one term consistently or note at first occurrence that they are synonymous.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening rhetorical concession by keeping the conditional clauses intact but making the sentence flow more naturally, so Tertullian's voice is clear and the reader can follow the argument without stumbling over the long subordinate structure.

notes.quote: May Christ Jesus our Lord permit me to say for the moment, whoever he is, of whatever god he is the son, of whatever substance he is man and God, of whatever faith he is the teacher, of whatever reward he is the promiser
notes.why: Long conditional clause with 'whoever he is' reads as if Tertullian doubts Christ's identity; likely a rhetorical concession but reads as garbled.
notes.fix: Note this is a rhetorical device: granting the opponent's premises for the sake of argument.
